description: C# and Razor (.cshtml/.razor) for VSCodium: IntelliSense, go to definition and tag helpers from Microsoft's roslyn-language-server, a Solution Explorer, F5 on launch profiles, and a bundled MIT-licensed .NET debugger.
command.addLaunchProfiles: Add the Startup Project to Run and Debug
command.searchEverywhere: Search (code, files, types, members, text, features)
config.solution: Solution (.sln/.slnx) to load. Empty: the first one found in the workspace.
config.serverPath: Path to Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.LanguageServer.dll. Empty: the one under the extension's server/ folder.
config.debuggerPath: Path to the debug adapter (Passenger.DebugAdapter(.exe)). Empty: the one under the extension's debugger/ folder.
config.razorViewsInDesignTime: Give the language server's Razor every .cshtml even when a project sets RazorCompileOnBuild=false (only the server's design-time builds change; your builds don't).
config.runMicrosoftConfigurations: Run launch.json configurations of type coreclr (Microsoft's C# extension) and dotnet (C# Dev Kit) on CSharpShooter's debugger.
config.runMicrosoftConfigurations.auto: When the extension that owns the type (C# for coreclr, C# Dev Kit for dotnet) is not installed or is disabled.
config.runMicrosoftConfigurations.always: Always, even with Microsoft's extensions installed.
config.runMicrosoftConfigurations.never: Never: those configurations need Microsoft's debugger.
config.taskRunner.projectOpenBindings: Start the tasks a gulpfile binds to Project Open (/// <binding ProjectOpened='...' />) as the workspace opens, as Visual Studio does. A run .vscode/tasks.json starts as the folder opens (runOn: folderOpen, the same gulp task in the same folder) is stopped, and the task runs in the Task Runner, its output in a console tab there.
config.taskRunner.buildBindings: Run a gulpfile's Before Build, After Build and Clean bindings around CSharpShooter's builds (F5, Solution Explorer). Off by default: a project that runs gulp from its .csproj when built outside Visual Studio (BuildingInsideVisualStudio != true) would run it twice.
config.askToTrustDevCertificate: Before F5 of a launch profile with an https URL, ask to trust ASP.NET Core's HTTPS development certificate when it is not trusted (dotnet dev-certs https --trust), as Visual Studio asks. Turned off by 'Don't ask me again'.
config.launchProfilesInLaunchJson: Put 'CSharpShooter' in .vscode/launch.json, so the Run and Debug dropdown has Visual Studio's start button: F5 on it runs the startup project with its active profile, chosen from the status bar. VS Code lists only launch.json's configurations there.
config.launchProfilesInLaunchJson.ask: Ask once per workspace when launch.json lacks it.
config.launchProfilesInLaunchJson.never: Never add it (the projects' profiles stay under '.NET (CSharpShooter)...' in Select and Start Debugging).
config.solutionSearch.fileContents: Solution Explorer's search also looks in the files' contents (ripgrep), as Visual Studio's 'Search within file contents'. Off by default, as there: only names.
config.uiLanguage: Language of CSharpShooter's own texts (notifications, status bar, Solution Explorer, Search, Publish, visualizer, Task Runner Explorer). auto: VS Code's display language. Command titles, view names and these descriptions always follow VS Code's display language.
config.uiLanguage.auto: VS Code's display language (Polish for Polish, English otherwise).
config.uiLanguage.pl: Polish, with Visual Studio's own Polish words.
debugger.label: .NET (CSharpShooter)
debugger.program: The app's .dll or apphost .exe; leave it out when 'project' is given.
debugger.project: A .csproj to build and run: its program comes from MSBuild (TargetPath), as VS's F5.
debugger.launchProfile: A profile of the project's Properties/launchSettings.json: its environment, URLs (ASPNETCORE_URLS), arguments and browser. IISExpress profiles run on Kestrel at the IIS Express URLs.
debugger.build: Build the project before it starts.
debugger.hotReload: Hot Reload: C#, .razor and .cshtml edits saved while the program runs under the debugger go into it without a restart. On by default for a Debug build.
debugger.launchBrowser: Open the browser when a profile asks for it, once the app listens.
debugger.startupProject: Run the startup project (status bar, Solution Explorer: Set as Startup Project) with its active launch profile (its .csproj.user's ActiveDebugProfile, as Visual Studio keeps it), as VS's F5.
debugger.framework: Target framework of a multi-targeted project (its .csproj.user's ActiveDebugFramework for the startup project).
config.visualStudioKeybindings: Visual Studio's keys, as Microsoft's Visual Studio Keymap has them (Ctrl+Shift+B build, F9/Ctrl+Shift+F9 breakpoints, Ctrl+F10 run to cursor, Ctrl+K Ctrl+D format, Ctrl+R Ctrl+R rename, Ctrl+- / Ctrl+Shift+- back and forward, Ctrl+L cut line...), with Ctrl+, and Ctrl+T on CSharpShooter's Search, Ctrl+Shift+F on its Find in Files and Ctrl+Alt+L on its Solution Explorer. Off: VS Code's own keys.
command.refactor.pullMembersUp: Pull Members Up to Base Type...
command.refactor.pushMembersDown: Push Members Down to Derived Types...
